items: Audit Your Physical Work Zone: Designate one specific surface as your permanent work location and commit to using only that spot during work hours because your brain needs a consistent spatial cue to enter focus mode.

Audit Your Physical Work Zone: Create visual separation between your work zone and rest zone using a folding screen, curtain, or specific chair that you only occupy during work hours to signal to your nervous system which mode is active.
Audit Your Physical Work Zone: Remove all non-work items from your designated work surface so your desk signals "focus mode" the moment you sit down and your eyes don't catch distractions.

Audit Your Physical Work Zone: Walk through your home and identify every visual cue that currently pulls you toward non-work activities like the couch, TV, or laundry pile so you know what to avoid during work hours.

Enforce Equipment Boundaries: Store all work equipment in a designated drawer or bag at the end of each workday so your workspace visually transforms into non-work space and creates a mental off-switch.

Enforce Equipment Boundaries: Put your laptop in a bag, charger in a drawer, and notebook on a shelf every single day because the physical act of packing away work signals to your brain that the workday is complete.

Enforce Equipment Boundaries: Never work from bed, even once, to prevent your brain from rewiring sleep associations into alertness associations which would then make both sleeping and working harder the next day.

Enforce Equipment Boundaries: Close and shelve your notebook completely at the end of each day and physically walk away from your work surface to reinforce that the workspace belongs to work, not to the rest of your life.

Replace Lost Accountability: Schedule home tasks like dishes, laundry, and bonsai trimming at specific times rather than doing them whenever they catch your attention because they're always available and will always seem more appealing than difficult work.

Replace Lost Accountability: Create visible project deadlines with concrete check-in points so you replace the ambient pressure that offices naturally provide with something tangible you can see and feel.

Replace Lost Accountability: Set timers and use time-blocking for your work tasks so "eventually" stops being your only deadline and you build the same temporal urgency that walking past a colleague's desk used to create.

Replace Lost Accountability: Establish a daily transition ritual between home life and work life using the same sequence of actions every morning so your brain learns to recognize the pattern as a signal to engage focus mode.
